output.title: Why subscription sprawl survives in small teams
output.body:
Subscription sprawl usually survives because it sits inside work that no one wants to own: audit, renew, cancel, repeat. The owner signs up for a tool, the monthly or quarterly check gets pushed into the back-office pile, and the list slowly becomes invisible. That is the real problem. Not the software, the visibility.

For a 1–10 person business, I would treat this as a workflow decision, not a cleanup project. The practical question is simple: can you list every active subscription and its renewal date right now? If not, start with a one-time manual audit. Do not automate a messy list. If yes, the next decision is whether you want a simple renewal alert, a central searchable register, or just a quarterly review that keeps the list honest.

That is the sort of bounded problem Bareni looks for: a repeatable workflow, a clear owner, and a control that stays human for anything involving cancellation or payment. If the list is already small and tidy, a spreadsheet may be enough. If it is messy, audit first, then decide whether a workflow with AI plus a spreadsheet is worth building. The build stays technical; the decision does not.
